title: Microsoft Teams: express face enrollment from meeting video for Teams Rooms recognition
summary: The before-rollout checklist directs administrators to a command that disables face enrollment when it tells them to inspect current settings. The roadmap facts and the related enrollment and room-recognition controls are supported, but that instruction must be corrected before publication.

claims.claim: Enrolled users can be recognised in supported Teams Rooms experiences.
claims.quote: Once enrolled, users can be recognized in supported Teams Rooms experiences

claims.claim: The roadmap links recognition to identifying people in the room and improving Copilot and recap experiences.
claims.quote: helping identify who is in the room and improving downstream meeting experiences such as Copilot and recap

claims.claim: No dedicated Learn page explicitly identifies itself as documentation for this roadmap item; the enrollment overview describes express face enrollment generally.
claims.quote: Searched: "express face enrollment" Teams admin policy default license eligible meetings. Opened voice-and-face-recognition and Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy; neither explicitly identifies roadmap item 570846.

claims.claim: Learn describes express enrollment using voice and images and videos of the user's face from Teams meetings.
claims.quote: a user can create their voice and face profile by "express enrollment" using their voice and images and videos of their face from Teams meetings

claims.claim: Active enrollment is a manual experience reached through Settings > Recognition in the Teams app.
claims.quote: Enrollment starts in the Teams app: users go to Settings > Recognition and, depending on how their Enterprise administrator has enabled the feature for them, opt in to either express enrollment or active enrollment.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Teams audio and video used to create profiles through express enrollment are not retained after the call.
claims.quote: If users enroll via express enrollment, Teams audio and video used to create voice and face profiles aren't retained after the end of the Teams call.

claims.claim: The recognition face profile is biometric data.
claims.quote: Voice and face recognition only works if end users have completed enrollment by creating their biometric profiles in Teams.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Teams Rooms face recognition identifies enrolled users appearing on camera.
claims.quote: Face recognition: Uses an enrolled user's face profile to identify them when they appear on camera in a meeting room.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Recognised users' contributions are attributed in transcriptions, meeting recaps and Copilot experiences.
claims.quote: When an enrolled user joins meetings from a Teams Room, their contributions are accurately attributed in transcriptions, meeting recaps, and Copilot experiences.

claims.claim: The existing EnrollVoice setting is enabled by default.
claims.quote: -EnrollVoice: Default value: Enabled

claims.claim: The existing EnrollFace setting is enabled by default.
claims.quote: -EnrollFace: Default value: Enabled

claims.claim: Learn says the existing PassiveVoiceEnrollment setting is enabled by default.
claims.quote: The new policy includes three distinct settings which are enabled by default
claims.fix: After the defaults sentence, add: 'The Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy reference qualifies PassiveVoiceEnrollment: organisations that previously disabled EnrollVoice receive a one-time matching state for PassiveVoiceEnrollment when express voice enrollment launches.' The reference is https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamsaipolicy.

claims.claim: Microsoft retains an enrolled user's profile subject to its retention policies while the Teams account is active.
claims.quote: When a user is enrolled in the feature and has an active Teams account, Microsoft, on behalf of the user's organization, retains their voice and face profiles in accordance with the following retention policies.

claims.claim: A voice and face profile unused for one year is removed automatically.
claims.quote: In addition, a voice and face profile that isn't used for one year is removed automatically.

claims.claim: The user's profile is removed within 90 days after the organisation deletes the Teams account.
claims.quote: If the organization deletes the user's Teams account, the user's voice and face profile is removed within 90 days of the Teams account being deleted.

claims.claim: The separate Face Recognition device setting defaults to Off, so enrollment alone does not enable room recognition.
claims.quote: | Face Recognition | Off | Users with enrolled face profile are identified with their face when using this device. Others are distinguished as meeting participants. |

claims.claim: Face recognition requires a supported camera or a Teams Rooms on Windows device with Cloud IntelliFrame enabled.
claims.quote: Face recognition requires a supported camera or Teams Rooms on Windows devices with Cloud IntelliFrame enabled.

claims.claim: Teams Rooms on Windows supports face recognition.
claims.quote: Teams Rooms on Windows | Voice recognition: Supported | Face recognition: Supported

claims.claim: Teams Rooms on Android does not support face recognition.
claims.quote: Teams Rooms on Android | Voice recognition: Supported | Face recognition: Not supported

claims.quote: Enterprise administrators can't export end-user voice or face enrollment data from the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: Enrollment data export remains under the end user's control.
claims.quote: Export of enrollment data remains under the end user's control and within the user experience.

claims.claim: Learn describes enrollment generally as available only up to GCC, not in GCC High or DoD.
claims.quote: No, voice and face enrollments are currently available only up to GCC and aren't available in GCCH or DOD environments.

claims.claim: Users can delete their profile at any time in Teams desktop, including after an administrator disables enrollment.

claims.claim: The enrollment overview does not specify an enrollment licence requirement.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams express face enrollment licensing pricing biometric recognition profile license. Read the enrollment overview in full: it identifies Teams Enterprise as the product context but gives no enrollment licence requirement.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a price specific to express face enrollment.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams express face enrollment licensing pricing biometric recognition profile license. Read enrollment overview and People Recognition; checked Teams Premium licensing for enrollment, recognition, biometric, express and face; no price found.

claims.claim: The enrollment overview documents no meter for express face enrollment at the time of writing.

claims.claim: People Recognition on Teams Rooms devices requires a Teams Rooms Pro licence, separately from any unconfirmed enrollment entitlement.
claims.quote: This feature is exclusive to Microsoft Teams Rooms devices with a Teams Rooms Pro license.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not defined which meetings are eligible for the planned express face enrollment feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "express face enrollment" Teams admin policy default license eligible meetings. Read roadmap and enrollment overview; neither defines eligible meetings for the planned face-enrollment feature.

claims.claim: The enrollment overview addresses Enterprise administrators.
claims.quote: Enterprise administrators can manage voice and face enrollment by using the CsTeamsAIPolicy.

claims.claim: Face enrollment has no language requirement.
claims.quote: There's no language requirement for face enrollment.

claims.claim: The enrollment overview does not identify a specific administrator role required to edit Teams AI policies.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams AI policy Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy administrator role permissions. Read enrollment overview and Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy; the overview uses Enterprise administrators without specifying an RBAC role.

claims.claim: No admin UI is documented for setting the EnrollFace Teams AI policy value; the policy is PowerShell-only.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams face enrollment EnrollFace Teams admin center PowerShell express face enrollment setting. Opened enrollment overview: 'You can access this policy only through Microsoft PowerShell.' Copilot overview search excerpt likewise says no Teams admin center setting.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy -Identity Global -EnrollFace Disabled is a MicrosoftTeams PowerShell command that disables the Global EnrollFace value.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy -Identity Global -EnrollFace Disabled
Set Teams AI policy "EnrollFace" value to "Disabled" for global as default.

claims.claim: EnrollFace controls access to face enrollment in Teams app settings and is described as allowing active enrollment.
claims.quote:
EnrollFace controls user access to user face enrollment in the Teams app settings.
Enabling these settings will allow your users in your organization the ability to enroll using active enrollment.

claims.claim: Teams AI enrollment policies can govern specific users or groups.
claims.quote: Enterprise administrators can turn on or off use of voice and face recognition and voice and face enrollment for specific users or groups using the Teams AI Policy.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; controls[1].api; summary; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: A dedicated express face enrollment switch and its UI or automation are not documented, and EnrollFace applicability to this planned flow is unconfirmed.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams face enrollment EnrollFace Teams admin center PowerShell express face enrollment setting. Read enrollment overview and Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy: EnrollFace is described as manual enrollment; PassiveVoiceEnrollment is express voice; no dedicated express-face switch.

claims.quote:
Log in to the Teams Pro Management Portal.
Select Rooms.
Select Settings followed by the Recognition tab
Enable Configure with device settings

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <PolicyName> -roomPeopleNameUserOverride Off disables video-based identification through the meeting-policy configuration.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity PolicyName -roomAttributeUserOverride Attribute -roomPeopleNameUserOverride On
roomPeopleNameUserOverride | Control the video-based user identification in meeting rooms. | Off - The room won't send video for identification.

claims.claim: Meeting-policy-based room recognition configuration will be retired in the future.

claims.quote: We recommend using device-level settings because meeting policy-based configuration will be retired in the future.

claims.claim: PassiveVoiceEnrollment controls express voice enrollment.

claims.quote: Searched: "express face enrollment" Teams admin policy default license eligible meetings. Read the full Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy syntax and parameter sections: EnrollFace, EnrollVoice, PassiveVoiceEnrollment, SpeakerAttributionBYOD, Description and Identity.

claims.claim: Administrators can view end-user enrollment status in Teams admin center.

claims.claim: Administrators can delete end-user voice and face profiles and enrollment data in Teams admin center.

claims.claim: The cited enrollment overview names Teams admin center for enrollment data management but supplies no menu path.

claims.claim: The Teams admin center enrollment-data-management capability does not change default feature availability or enrollment behaviour.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, first bullet
claims.claim: Administrators can read current enrollment policy values using the first controls row.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy -Identity Global -EnrollFace Disabled
Set Teams AI policy "EnrollFace" value to "Disabled" for global as default.
claims.fix: Replace the first Before rollout bullet with: 'Inspect the Global and any custom Teams AI policies with Get-CsTeamsAIPolicy; do not run the first controls row's disable command merely to inspect settings.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/get-csteamsaipolicy, which states that the cmdlet retrieves all Teams AI policies for the tenant.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes recognition and identification rather than autonomous actions on the user's behalf.
claims.quote: Once enrolled, users can be recognized in supported Teams Rooms experiences, helping identify who is in the room and improving downstream meeting experiences such as Copilot and recap.

claims.where: rationale: impact; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified who receives a prompt for the planned feature or when.
claims.quote: Searched: "express face enrollment" Teams admin policy default license eligible meetings. Read roadmap, enrollment overview and Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy; no express-face rollout prompt audience or timing specified.

claims.claim: The effect of disabling the planned express face setting on already-created profiles is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams face enrollment EnrollFace Teams admin center PowerShell express face enrollment setting. Read roadmap, enrollment overview and Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy: user deletion after disabling is documented, but no planned express-face switch or its profile-deletion semantics.

claims.claim: The supplied roadmap and cited documentation do not state that this planned item's arrival changes existing behaviour automatically.
claims.quote: Searched: "express face enrollment" Teams admin policy default license eligible meetings. Read roadmap, enrollment overview and Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy; none describes an automatic behaviour change on arrival for roadmap item 570846.
